A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Polar Sparsity and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream accuracy, activation statistics, kernel measurements, and decoding throughput and latency experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds instruction-tuned benchmark evaluations, Mistral results, and measurements across GPU families.

M1.justification: The router architectures, 99% recall calibration, dense QKV projections, selective head/group attention, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. The loss and optimizer newly mentioned in Section 4.1 were already documented in v1 Appendix C; foregrounding Selective Head Attention does not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU-PRO and LongBench-e evaluations for instruction-tuned models (Table 2), substantially extending task coverage to more challenging reasoning and long-context generative evaluation. The nine original downstream benchmarks and WikiText-2 usage are retained.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 3 contain the same comparators: Probe Pruning, ReLUfication, ProSparse, CATS, TEAL, GRIFFIN, and R-Sparse. Throughput comparisons retain dense inference and DejaVu-style sparsity; the added evaluations introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: v3 adds pretrained Mistral-7B and instruction-tuned Mistral-7B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Qwen-2.5-14B configurations, using 50% or 62.5% attention density. Appendix D extends kernel testing to A5000 and H100 GPUs at OPT-66B, batch size 64, and sequence length 1920. Existing training and throughput protocols are retained; greedy decoding is newly disclosed rather than shown to have changed.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 11 adds a hardware-sensitivity analysis testing whether selective-kernel latency scales with density across A5000, A100, and H100 GPUs. The OPT-30B activation-distribution panel from v1 Figure 7b is removed. The ReLU-LLaMA panel is relocated, while the router ablation, head-activation analysis, and other sensitivity studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions describe means and standard deviations for batch-activation statistics in Appendix B.1. v3 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive results in Tables 1–2: Mistral-7B averages 0.663 dense versus 0.657 sparse, and Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct scores 0.497 versus 0.457 on MMLU-PRO. Figure 11 adds GPU-specific latency curves, while the OPT-30B activation panel is removed. Shared benchmark scores and existing throughput findings are unchanged; these are additional results rather than same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The MLP union-set formulation, attention equations, and mathematical content of the algorithms are retained. The added prose definition of head sparsity is explanatory; no formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of batch-invariant attention sparsity, scalable contextual sparsity, and up to 2.2× acceleration with negligible accuracy loss. v3 foregrounds Selective Head Attention and names Qwen and Mistral as additional examples without changing the overarching contribution or novelty claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly identifies greedy decoding and contexts up to 16k tokens as evaluation boundaries, leaving beam search, speculative decoding, and million-token contexts untested. Section 5.1 extends the task-sensitivity discussion to MMLU-PRO. The explanation of GQA sensitivity is relocated from the evaluation section rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly discloses greedy decoding, identifies the FlashAttention implementation as Triton, and supplies hardware and workload details for the new cross-GPU experiment. Router-training hyperparameters and the code-access URL remain unchanged; the pipeline-parallel setup was already documented in v1 Appendix E.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for LongBench, MMLU-PRO, Mistral, LLaMA-2, and OPT. Positioning relative to earlier sparsity methods remains substantially unchanged, and the PowerInfer/Herd discussion moves from Section 2 to Appendix A.1.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, and conclusion receive localized rewrites emphasizing Selective Head Attention; Section 4.2 is retitled and several discussions move between sections and appendices. The conference header and acknowledgments also change, while the overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Selective Head Attention schematic, an instruction-tuned results table, and the cross-GPU kernel figure. Activation panels are regrouped between the main text and appendix, one OPT-30B panel is removed, and Table 1 is expanded and reformatted. Most existing plots are reused unchanged, with localized layout and caption revisions.

improvement.justification: The new instruction-tuned and long-context evaluations, GPU portability analysis, and explicit applicability limits strengthen evidence for practical use. The gain is limited by insufficiently qualified accuracy claims: Section 5.1 retains the within-1% characterization despite Table 2 showing MMLU-PRO drops of 2.5 percentage points for LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and 4 points for Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct.
